articles.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、AI agent & application
articles.summary: The iPhone maker appears to be building agents that can compete with the likes of Meta Muse, Instinct, Claude, and OpenAI Dots.
articles.full_text:
Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.

The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.” “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step.

It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.” The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.” TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year.

Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space.

It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the company is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.

The outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents.

In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.” Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.” Topics AI , AI agents , Apple , Meta , muse When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission .

articles.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: At the upgraded $83/share IPO price, Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million, while the company nabbed nearly $105 billion.
articles.full_text:
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders.

As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes.

It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74.

That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range.

So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though.

The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments.

The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.” With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting. $104.8 billion.

That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares).

In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day. 28% stake to Amazon and Google combined.

All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company.

Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity.

It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake.

Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

More than $1 trillion.

As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.

Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030.

And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.

All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future.

This was a huge IPO.

But it is a pricey business to run.

articles.full_text:
Tech AI News Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent Apple’s job listing describes an AI agent that can browse the web, work across apps, and call services.

Apple’s job listing describes an AI agent that can browse the web, work across apps, and call services. by Emma Roth Nov 19, 2026, 10:31 PM UTC Link Share Gift Photo by Allison Johnson / The Verge Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more.

Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services.

That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg , which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhone maker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta’s Muse , OpenAI’s Dots , Anthropic’s Duet , and Google’s Tasks .

Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.

Apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps.

It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities , as a report from Bloomberg suggests the company could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs.

This lines up with the company’s new job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.

Related Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers “People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.” With its upcoming iOS 27.3 update , Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.

articles.full_text:
Tech AI News Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free Tasks in Gemini allows the AI agent to call businesses on your behalf, purchase items with Google Pay, and more.

Tasks in Gemini allows the AI agent to call businesses on your behalf, purchase items with Google Pay, and more. by Emma Roth Nov 17, 2026, 6:58 PM UTC Link Share Gift Image: Google Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more.

Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as “Tasks” and making it free to use.

The feature, which is powered by Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.

Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager.

US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.

Google first introduced its Spark AI agent in May , but it was only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

The launch of tasks in Gemini brings Spark’s capabilities to all users in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India.

You can find tasks by opening Gemini and changing the toggle on the homepage from “Chat” to “Tasks.” Tasks in Gemini is just one of the many agentic AI features that have emerged over the past year, including Claude Duet, OpenAI’s Dots , and Meta’s Muse .

Google says Gemini will perform tasks in a “hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.” You can also provide instructions for Gemini while it completes tasks.

When performing more sensitive tasks, like purchasing an item, it will stop working and ask for your permission before following through.
